restrictions: Two distinct 128-byte one-block messages m(a), m(b) of sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1 (zero state, rate 136, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 5, full 256-bit digest). m(u) places the point u (lanes u0..u3) in lanes 1, 6, 11 = u0^K1, u1^K6, u0^u1^K11 and 4, 9, 14 = u2^K4, u3^K9, u2^u3^K14, the other lanes 0..15 the fixed constants K of proof.md Section 2 (set 56, trial 0); F(u) = SHA3-256-r6(m(u)) xor PD, and F(a) = F(b) with a != b is a collision of two distinct messages.

Distinguished-point parallel collision search (van Oorschot-Wiener) on F with 256 walks per step, the search of 2d74a370 and 2acfdbee: DP = image x < 708 x 2^135 (planes 145..255 zero and the 10 planes below them < 708; theta = 708 x 2^-121, H = 111.5324), no trail cut, replay cap 39,426,468,968,298,390,845,350,463,093,604,352 steps, at most 92,192 trails, a table of 23,048 words with four 64-bit records each (46 end bits and the trail number), and Tb = 535671131 x 2^91 steps. The common prefilter ORs planes 241..255; its hit handler ORs planes 145..240 and applies the unchanged ten-bit comparison. It aborts at hit 49,787,865,427,095,778,383,460,604,988,882,946, and one replay measures the stored trail by walking it to its DP.

One step of 256 walks is a generated bit-sliced straight line of 26,570 register operations (19,077 XOR, 3,906 AND, 2,750 OR, 837 NOT; no loads or stores): lazy per-row theta, per-row complement subsets and 10-gate chi rows, NOTs placed by a polarity plan, dead-code elimination, last-use allocation (step design after jungjipdo's 67f781f8, our own generator gen3.c, written round by round; proof.md Section 3).

Machine model (the declared prices of the cost model of this entry, proof.md Section 3.6; the benchmark fixes neither): a declared file of 2,192 registers of 256 bits, the convention of 67f781f8, its 70,144 bytes counted as memory, an operation on registers costing one word operation, every load and store of the other code charged; 5 bytes per straight-line instruction and 32 bytes per instruction of the other code (2,715 instructions, 86,880 bytes), PERM one unit. The revised prefilter is 14 five-byte OR instructions.

Memory at most 1,044,376 bytes < 2^20 (margin 4,200): registers 70,144, straight line plus prefilter 132,920, control 86,880, table 737,536, walk state 16,384, data 512. The packed fixed-capacity control constructor is bounded by 190,464 bytes. The straight-line generator phase, including its inherited 468,077-byte bound and the retained 86,950-byte control/prefilter output, is bounded by 555,027 bytes. Construction, generation and search are sequential phases.

Success at least 0.39 for one attempt over the fresh word rho, under the score-critical premise H_rand (our theory: over the algorithm's coin rho the program on the fixed target succeeds with at least the random-function probability of proof.md Section 5), with failure terms for a colliding pair with a trail of more than LRC evaluations, the trail limit, self-coincidence, starts and 46-bit key matches, and the hit-counter abort. For the 15-plane filter, each fresh step hits with conditional probability at most 1/128 and the inherited stopping-time bound still gives F5 < 2^-1000.

heuristics.statement: Premise H_rand (our theory): over the algorithm's coins, the program run on the fixed SHA3-256-r6 target (F(u) = SHA3-256-r6(m(u)) xor PD, with the linear-structure message embedding m of proof.md Section 2) succeeds with probability at least the probability computed in proof.md Section 5 for a uniformly random function F from 256-bit values to 256-bit values. The only coin of the algorithm is the uniform word rho; the target is fixed, and given rho the run is deterministic. The computation of Section 5 is made in the random-function model, where F is realised by lazy sampling (values at distinct inputs independent and uniform, a fresh point a distinguished point with probability 708 x 2^-121), and there one attempt succeeds with probability at least 0.39 after the failure terms. The premise is that the fixed target carries this probability over.
heuristics.scope: The fixed function F of proof.md Section 2 on the points of one attempt: about 0.997765 x 2^128 evaluations in 256 lockstep walks from starts rho + i, i < 92,192. Only the pair-coincidence rate among evaluated images and the distinguished-point rate enter the bound. The step program, the cost, the memory and the failure terms are derived, not assumed.
heuristics.extrapolation: Not an estimate of the success probability for the fixed target. Before either declared experiment, the program assembles and checks the revised 2,715-instruction control image and 14-OR prefilter, including 128 direct-versus-encoded handler-mask tests. rho-w22 runs the whole search with the claimed straight line at width 22 (every trial must return a 22-bit partial collision; an ideal random function needs 20.47 steps on average); proj-w256 runs eight chained full-width steps and tests 22-bit agreement among 2,048 iterates (model 0.3934 per trial). Inherited 32-bit-window checks appear in the proof; none establishes full-width random-function behavior.
heuristics.limitations: Our theory; no proof. No run reaches 2^128 and no full collision is claimed. The checks work at 22 and 32 bits (and 44 to 48 bits in rho length, on other constants). A pair-coincidence deficit eps costs about 0.5 log2(1/(1 - eps)) bits of time.
